title: manuscript-guard data dictionary
description: design/data_dictionary.yaml: one entry for each variable the study collects or reads, saying what it is, how it is coded and why it is there. Written at the design stage from the analysis plan, before the data are collected or read. G12 holds it to the plan; the data-quality checks hold the data to it. What the schema cannot say (unique names, references between entries, codes against their type) is checked by contracts/dictionary.py.

id.description: A form, dataset, instrument, code list or rule: lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

name.description: A variable's name as the data hold it: letters, digits, underscores and dots, starting with a letter. Capitals and dots are allowed because an existing dataset's columns may have them; the REDCap export refuses a name REDCap cannot take.

code.description: A value as the data hold it. Compared as text: 1 and "1" are one code.

bound.description: A number for a continuous or count variable; an ISO 8601 date, date and time, or time, in quotes for a time, for the others.

label.description: How the paper and the form name the variable.

definition.description: What the variable is, as it will be coded: precise enough that two people recording it from the same source record the same value.

type.description: The first five are the kinds the emitter's variable() declares and G15 reads.

question.description: The wording on the form or the survey, where it is not the label. A validated instrument's wording is copied from the licensed instrument, never written from memory.

values.description: The allowed codes of a binary, categorical or ordinal variable; an ordinal's in the order of its scale.

code_list.description: A list in code_lists, in place of values.

range.description: The plausible values, both bounds included.

missing.description: Codes that stand for a missing value, each with what it means: not asked, not known, refused.

required.description: A record without a value for it is incomplete. Where applies_if is given, only among the records it applies to.

applies_if.description: The variable is recorded only where another, coded variable holds one of these codes.

source.description: Where the value is read from: the participant, the medical record, a registry.

derived_from.description: The variables a derived variable is computed from.

derivation.description: How a derived variable is computed from its inputs.

item.description: The instrument's item this variable records.

system.description: MedDRA, CTCAE, ICD-10, ATC, LOINC, SNOMED CT or another published terminology.

code.description: Copied from the terminology, never from memory.

standard.description: A standard definition the variable follows.

reporting.description: The reporting-checklist items that need the variable: the guideline's name, then its item numbers.

reason.description: Why the variable is collected, where no planned result and no reporting item needs it.

pattern.description: For text and identifiers: a regular expression a value matches whole.

within_study_period.description: For dates: the value falls within study_period.

order.description: Each value is no greater than the next, where all are present.

unique.description: No two rows of their dataset hold the same values of these.

computed.description: The author's script finds the rows that break it.

datasets.description: The tables of a dataset in several parts, as a spontaneous reporting database is.

forms.description: The parts of the collection instrument, in order: the pages of a case report form, the sections of a survey, the parts of an extraction form.

citation.description: The citation key of the paper that validated it.

licence.description: The terms of use as the holder states them, or that they are not known and whom to ask.

instruments.description: The validated instruments the study uses: scales, questionnaires, grading systems.

code_lists.description: Lists of codes several variables share, each under its name.

variables.description: One entry for each variable, in the order of the form.

rules.description: What must hold across variables or rows. The data-quality checks read them.
